messages.content: The sofa arrived and it's in much worse condition than the listing made it seem. The scratches and discoloration are much more noticeable in person than in the photos.

I'm sorry you're disappointed, but the listing clearly described all the wear. I mentioned the armrest scratch, the cushion patina, and the color variation, and provided close-up photos of each. The sofa matches the description.
The photos didn't capture how worn the leather really feels. 'Good condition' should mean it looks presentable, not that it's visibly aged. For $2,200 this is unacceptable quality.

I understand expectations can differ from reality, but I was transparent about the condition. Every defect was listed and photographed. The price reflects the condition grade — a new Maxwell in this size is over $8,000. I don't think a refund is warranted here.
